title: Ultrasound determination of the course of the radial nerve in the upper arm region and its relationship to bony landmarks
summary:
Background:
The radial nerve spirals around the humerus and is particularly at risk during fractures or surgical procedures involving the upper arm. Previous anatomical studies were mostly conducted on cadavers or intraoperatively and therefore cannot be reliably transferred to surface anatomy. A preoperative, non-invasive prediction of the nerve’s course based on palpable bony landmarks could significantly improve surgical safety.

Research question:
Can the course of the radial nerve in the upper arm be reliably related to palpable bony landmarks using ultrasound, allowing its trajectory to be estimated preoperatively?

Methods:
In this prospective, controlled cross-sectional study, healthy adult volunteers will be examined. Defined bony landmarks are marked on both upper arms, and the radial nerve will be visualized sonographically at two predefined points. The distances between the nerve and the landmarks will be measured in millimeters and related to the individual humeral length.
To assess measurement reliability, a subset of participants will undergo a repeated measurement after at least 5 days by the same examiner (intrarater reliability), and selected participants will be examined a second time by a different examiner (interrater reliability).

Expected results:
The results will indicate whether the course of the radial nerve can be reliably predicted based on external anatomical landmarks and whether the measurement method is reproducible and independent of the examiner.
conditions: The study does not investigate a disease but examines normal anatomical conditions in healthy adult individuals. The aim is to determine the course of the radial nerve in the upper arm in order to better assess and prevent the risk of nerve injury during future surgeries or in cases of upper arm trauma.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy adult individuals aged 18 years or older

Ability to give informed consent and sign the written consent form

Anatomically normal upper arms on both sides (no prior surgery, trauma, or congenital abnormality)

Ability to remain in a prone position for approximately 30 minutes during examination

Reliable self-reported information regarding body height, weight, and handedness
Exclusion criteria:
Minors or individuals unable to provide informed consent

Previous surgery, fracture, or congenital malformation of the upper arm

Current or past inflammation, infection, or oncological disease in the examined region

Ambidextrous or retrained handedness

Physical or cognitive impairments that prevent adequate participation or accurate data collection
